UULTIS /PRODUCT NOTES / 3 MIN READ

Before you choose a piece.

A practical guide to using photographs, dimensions and technical documents together.

Uultis digital experience · Editorial guide

IN THIS ARTICLEMatch the name and version.Read every dimension in context.Keep the photograph nearby.Resolve missing information before ordering.

Match the name and version.

Start on the product page and open its technical sheet. Check that the document describes the piece and size you are considering. A collection may include related names or multiple variants; a shared name does not necessarily mean the same footprint.

Read every dimension in context.

Width, depth and height describe different parts of a piece. Check the drawing and units, rather than relying on the order of three numbers. For seating, look for seat dimensions where provided. For a table, consider how its base interacts with the chairs or seating beside it.

Keep the photograph nearby.

The photograph helps you interpret a drawing: where the supports sit, how the edge is shaped and which areas are upholstered. In the Room Studio, open “Compare with the product photo” while exploring the interactive model. The image remains the reference for details the study may simplify.

Resolve missing information before ordering.

If a dimension, material or care instruction is not documented, ask the team. Keep the product name, chosen version and a link to the technical sheet in your enquiry. The contact page prepares an email draft that you can review before sending.
